To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
experience formed at different ontogenetic stages is different in terms of pleasantness judgment and emotion intensity.
the pleasantness judgment takes longer and generates less intense emotions when experience is related to vision, skin sensations and hearing than when experience is related by taste and olfaction.

early-formed experience related predominantly to vision, hearing, skin sensations and taste differs from late-formed experience related predominantly olfaction and that the dynamics of skin conductance corresponded to pleasantness of reported emotion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between language acquisition, sensory modalities, and individual experience.
the ontogenesis of the human sensory experience.
the relationship between language acquisition and the formation of individual experience.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pleasantness judgment is more difficult for early-formed experience related predominantly to vision, hearing, and skin sensations and that this experience is less intense, less differentiated and less pleasant than that related predominantly to taste and olfaction.

early-formed experience related mainly to skin sensations, taste and olfaction is characterized by a higher degree of integration and a lower degree of differentiation than later-formed experience related mainly vision and hearing.

the pleasantness judgment is faster and more emotional when experience is related to early-formed senses (olfaction and taste), and the pleasantness judgment takes longer and is less emotional when experience is described by later-formed senses (vision, hearing and skin sensitivity).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
experience related to vision, olfaction and hearing is formed earlier in ontogeny than experience related to taste and skin sensations.
experience formed early in ontogeny has a more general and more positive character than experience formed later in ontogeny.
the development of the sensory modalities and of language is closely related.
The main takeaway from our work is that

experience related to olfaction is the most intense, positive and differentiated, experience related to taste is the second most differentiated and experience related to skin sensation is the least differentiated.
the pleasantness of mental experience related to different senses and acquired at different stages of development is modulated by the dynamics of skin electrical resistance.
the pleasantness judgment is a reliable indicator of the intensity of emotions.
